principles: An infrastructure failure must never be presented as a data difference
Fix the observed defect and its identical latent siblings together
A limit that can be reached must be measurable before it is reached
A growth cliff must end in a shipped consequence, not an opinion
drivers: No story in the repository can enter TEST until this is fixed
The failure is silent and its message names the wrong cause
The artifact grows with the configured command count, which grew seventy-nine percent in one day

options.name: explicit-ceiling-and-honest-error
pros: Fixes the observed defect and its latent siblings in one pass
Makes the next ceiling failure diagnosable in minutes rather than hours
cons: Moves the cliff rather than removing it unless paired with a growth disposition

options.name: bound-the-artifact-only
pros: Removes the growth cliff at its source
cons: Leaves every other blob read carrying the same latent limit
Larger design surface than a bugfix story should carry alone

options.name: raise-ceiling-only
cons: Reproduces the identical failure at a higher number
No regression, so it returns silently
Leaves the misleading message that made this expensive

rationale: Raising the ceiling alone reproduces the same failure at a higher number with no regression and no honest message, which is precisely how this defect survived undetected. Bounding the artifact alone leaves every sibling blob read carrying the identical latent limit and does nothing for diagnosability. The chosen option fixes the defect and its siblings, makes the next occurrence diagnosable, and is paired with a binding disposition for aggregate growth plus a near-limit advisory so the cliff is marked rather than merely moved.

preMortem.scenario: Ceiling added only to the helper observed to fail
preMortem.trigger: An implementer patches isolatedBlobHash and stops there because that is the one the transcript named
preMortem.consequence: isolatedGit and treeBlobHash reproduce the identical defect from a different call site
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-001 requires auditing every blob and tree read in the module, not only the observed one

preMortem.scenario: The catch is replaced but still collapses two distinct cases
preMortem.trigger: The repair focuses on the message text rather than on what the caller can distinguish
preMortem.consequence: The message improves without becoming diagnostic, so the next occurrence costs the same hours
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-002 requires blob genuinely absent and blob could not be read to remain distinguishable, with the underlying error surfaced

preMortem.scenario: The regression uses a fixture below the limit
preMortem.trigger: A small fixture is chosen for speed, as every existing test in this area did
preMortem.consequence: It passes on the unfixed tree and proves nothing, which is exactly why the defect was never caught
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-003 requires a blob above 1048576 bytes and demonstration that it fails on the pre-fix tree

preMortem.scenario: CHK-004 closes with a written opinion and no shipped consequence
preMortem.trigger: Urgency to unblock the repository makes the rationale branch attractive as an escape rather than a decision
preMortem.consequence: The unexamined growth cliff this story exists to end is recreated at a higher number
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-004 requires shipping whichever branch is chosen, and the rationale branch must name a concrete successor change rather than a vague intention

preMortem.scenario: The advisory threshold is measured against the wrong ceiling
preMortem.trigger: The one-mebibyte figure is the memorable number from the incident, so it is reused as the denominator
preMortem.consequence: The advisory fires at the wrong point and either never warns or warns constantly
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-005 measures the fraction against the ceiling this story sets, not against any external default
